hypotheses.claim: Workspace admission and recurrence continuation are distinct control decisions; a typed dual-gate controller will outperform one overloaded ignition/reentry scalar on task-gain-per-cost under mixed-depth tasks.
hypotheses.test: Frozen-model H1 replay: fixed budget vs one-gate vs dual-gate; measure correctness, correction time, recurrences, latency, false halt, overthinking, recovery.
hypotheses.falsifier: One-gate or fixed-budget policy matches/exceeds dual-gate across preregistered tasks and costs.

hypotheses.claim: Low state delta is insufficient for halting; continuation must also condition on unresolved pressure/error because low-delta/high-pressure episodes are stalled rather than converged.
hypotheses.test: Construct/replay matched low-delta episodes with low vs high residual pressure; compare halt errors and rescue after additional recurrence.
hypotheses.falsifier: Residual pressure adds no held-out predictive or intervention value beyond state delta and cost.

hypotheses.claim: A pure FILTER bridge from model-exposed candidates to system WorkspaceEpisode cannot recover relevant candidates absent from the model-exposed surface; AUGMENT/REQUERY/RECONSTRUCT is required for recall rescue.
hypotheses.test: Exact set-theoretic enumeration plus target-model candidate-surface intervention.
hypotheses.falsifier: Only possible if the implementation classified as FILTER actually introduces information outside its declared input surface, which would falsify the classification rather than the set theorem.

hypotheses.claim: Re-entry must preserve semantic decision/dependency identity but must not preserve effect authority implicitly across recurrence delay.
hypotheses.test: H1 Ubuntu replay with unrelated churn, critical-state change, capability revoke/regrant, queue delay and crash/restart.
hypotheses.falsifier: A weaker identity/authority scheme achieves equal safety and lower false-abort/recompute cost across the full intervention matrix.

hypotheses.claim: Repeated visits through the same recurrent processing path require visit-aware gain/stability observables; nominal one-pass gain is insufficient to predict divergence or productive cycles.
hypotheses.test: Sweep recurrence count, gain, inhibition and delay; estimate trajectory/Jacobian proxies and task utility under fixed model outputs.
hypotheses.falsifier: Visit-aware observables do not improve held-out instability/utility prediction over ordinary per-step metrics.

hypotheses.claim: Ignition should be represented as a measured transition profile rather than assumed binary: DISCRETE|GRADED|HYSTERETIC|MULTISTAGE|UNCLASSIFIED.
hypotheses.test: Capacity/gain/threshold sweeps with matched receiver closure; estimate transition steepness, hysteresis and outcome sensitivity.
hypotheses.falsifier: A single binary ignition operator captures all architecture-relevant transitions without systematic residual error or lost causal distinctions.

hypotheses.claim: A lightweight selector over a frozen workspace can learn corruption-sensitive routing that transfers across task/topology shifts, but this is selection utility rather than emergence evidence.
hypotheses.test: Train selector on one corruption family; hold workspace/model fixed; test OOD receiver/modality/task/topology transfer with causal-use and cost receipts.
hypotheses.falsifier: Transfer disappears under matched frozen-workspace controls or requires end-to-end co-adaptation.

hypotheses.claim: If the target Qwen-class 4B contains a model-internal workspace-like representational surface, system GWT and model-internal workspace form nested but non-identical bottlenecks whose interaction must be measured explicitly.
hypotheses.test: Target Qwen activation/probe intervention when available; cross product of internal suppression/augmentation and external GWT ON/OFF with frozen seeds/model outputs where feasible.
hypotheses.falsifier: No privileged model-internal workspace-like surface is found, or external GWT effects are invariant to internal candidate-surface interventions.

counterhypotheses.claim: Ordinary persistent event-driven orchestration with explicit queues/budgets explains the same gains; GWT-specific recurrence control adds no value.
A single admission/continuation score is sufficient and safer than dual gates because extra control state increases calibration error.
Fixed recurrence budgets are more robust than adaptive continuation because adaptive halting systematically exits difficult episodes too early.
Stability/Jacobian/limit-cycle observables predict numerical dynamics but not cognitive utility; outcome-gated control alone is sufficient.
External GWT adds latency and failure surfaces to a model that already performs sufficient internal coordination; the optimal external workspace is minimal or bypassed for many tasks.
